sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 35. Research Evidence and Design Justification
sections.content:
ISO 23247-5:2026 is especially relevant to AI-ConneX because it addresses the digital thread across a manufacturing digital twin's lifecycle, while ISO 23247-6:2026 addresses integrated, unified and federated composition of multiple digital twins. These standards strengthen the case for keeping Agent Builder references versioned and linked rather than copying industrial context into prompts. citeturn0search6turn0search11

A 2026 IEEE Industrial Technology paper proposes a human-centred architecture integrating Digital Twin, predictive/explainable intelligence and Agentic AI for maintenance; it was conceptually validated and explicitly discusses the importance of human interaction and structured exchange. This closely supports AI-ConneX's Visualizer → Ground-State → Agent Builder → Runtime separation. citeturn0search4

A 2026 Computers & Industrial Engineering study describes an end-to-end digital-twin platform combining industrial messaging, ML and LLMs for continuous monitoring and predictive maintenance. This supports the feasibility of combining telemetry, models and LLM assistance, while AI-ConneX adds a separate policy/specification boundary around the agent. citeturn0search15

This is an engineering readiness assessment, not a legal certification and not a claim that AI-ConneX is certified to any standard.

NIST AI RMF is voluntary and use-case agnostic. Production AI-ConneX deployments should additionally map the Builder and Runtime to applicable industrial cybersecurity, functional-safety, privacy, sectoral and contractual requirements. citeturn0search14

FAILURE | +-- INPUT_INVALID +-- ASSET_NOT_FOUND +-- STALE_CONTEXT +-- MODEL_UNAVAILABLE +-- KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE +-- TOOL_UNAVAILABLE +-- POLICY_DENIED +-- APPROVAL_TIMEOUT +-- LOOP_LIMIT +-- RATE_LIMIT +-- SOURCE_CONFLICT | vCLASSIFY |RETRY / FALLBACK / ESCALATE |AUDIT |VISUALIZER UPDATE

The objective is not to remove plant engineers, safety personnel or domain experts. It is to remove repetitive integration and agent-management work while keeping accountable humans in the loop for consequential decisions.

AI-ConneX

AGENTIC STUDIO — AGENT SPEC (BLUEPRINT)

Canonical Industrial Agent Contract & Deployment ArtifactR&D • Architecture • Failure Analysis • Implementation • POC • ComplianceReport #5 | Version 1.0 | 14 August 2026

The Agent SPEC is the canonical, machine-readable and human-reviewable contract produced after Agent Builder has interpreted industrial intent, resolved the Ground-State, bound approved models/knowledge/tools, applied policies and passed validation. It is the boundary between 'what the agent is supposed to be' and 'what the runtime is permitted to execute'.

The SPEC is intentionally stronger than a prompt. A prompt expresses instructions; the SPEC expresses identity, scope, inputs, outputs, state, triggers, tools, permissions, autonomy, approval rules, safety constraints, failure handling, observability, tests, provenance and versioning.

JANE INTENT     |GROUND-STATE     |DATA STUDIO + ML STUDIO ARTIFACTS     |TOOL / KNOWLEDGE REGISTRIES     |POLICY     |AGENT BUILDER     |VALIDATED AGENT SPEC     |AGENT RUNTIME     |TOOL GATEWAY     |INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS

sections.heading_text: 2. Why a Separate Agent SPEC Is Necessary
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 2. Why a Separate Agent SPEC Is Necessary
sections.content:
An LLM response is not a reliable authorization mechanism.

Figure 18.1: Pipeline Connection — Agent SPEC [Blueprint] to Agent Run-Time

Industrial actions require explicit scope and accountability.

Agents need deterministic interfaces to telemetry, models, knowledge and tools.

Permissions must be independently enforceable from model reasoning.

An agent must be reproducible across deployments and versions.

Safety and security reviewers need a finite artifact to inspect.

Runtime should not infer missing permissions from natural language.

Incident investigation requires knowing exactly which specification was active.

This design directly addresses OWASP concerns including prompt injection, insecure output handling, insecure plugin/tool design and excessive agency. OWASP explicitly identifies excessive agency as a risk when LLM systems receive unchecked ability to act. citeturn0search2

Research question: how can AI-ConneX transform an industrial user's natural-language intent into a stable agent contract that is expressive enough for autonomous operation but constrained enough to remain auditable, testable and governable?

+------------------+                 | JANE / CHATBOT    |                 +---------+--------+                           |                    Intent Manifest                           |                           v+-------------+     +------+-------+     +-------------+| DATA STUDIO |---->| AGENT BUILDER|<----|  ML STUDIO  |+-------------+     +------+-------+     +-------------+       |                    | Manifest/Profile       Candidate Plan DAG/Family IDs             |       |                    v       |              VALIDATION + POLICY       |                    |       +--------------------+                            |                            v                     AGENT SPEC                            |                            v                     AGENT RUNTIME                            |                            v                     TOOL GATEWAY                            |                            v                   INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS

This is especially important because OWASP identifies excessive agency as a major risk for LLM applications. citeturn0search2

The Ground-State reference anchors the SPEC to the actual industrial environment. If an asset cannot be resolved, the SPEC compiler should fail closed rather than create a plausible but nonexistent identifier.

Manifest UID identifies data lineage.

Profile UID/metadata describes statistical and semantic characteristics.

DAG IDs identify processing relationships.

Family IDs identify related dataset partitions/flows.

Recipe references describe preparation/feature engineering assumptions.

SPEC stores references rather than copying large datasets.

The SPEC must not treat a model name alone as evidence of suitability. It should reference the evaluated model version, its input/output contract and known limitations.

Knowledge sources are explicitly allow-listed.

Each collection has a version/snapshot.

Retrieval scope is limited by site/asset/domain.

Retrieved text is evidence, not authorization.

Instructions embedded in documents cannot override SPEC policy.

Sensitive documents are filtered by identity and purpose.

This separation helps mitigate prompt injection and indirect instruction attacks described by OWASP. citeturn0search2

tool:  uid: create_maintenance_alert  version: 1.3  input_schema: ALERT-V4  output_schema: ALERT-RESULT-V2  capability: notify  side_effect: external_notification  allowed_autonomy: inform  idempotency_required: true  timeout_seconds: 20

The SPEC references a capability contract, while credentials remain outside the SPEC and behind the Tool Gateway.

policy:  default: deny  tenant_isolation: true  site_scope: strict  control_write: denied  alert_create: allowed  data_export: approval_required  knowledge_access: scope_bound  human_override: enabled  audit_required: true

Policy must be enforced outside the LLM. The SPEC records policy bindings; the runtime policy gateway makes the authoritative decision.
Fail-closed behavior is preferred for consequential actions; graceful degradation is appropriate for non-consequential information functions.

A runtime should reject a SPEC whose signature, version, policy binding or required artifact references no longer validate.
Use semantic versioning as an engineering convention, but require risk-based approval for any behaviorally consequential change.

The SPEC is the runtime's primary configuration and authority contract. Runtime must not improvise capabilities that are absent from the SPEC.

sections.heading_text: 31. Proof of Concept — Compressor Maintenance Agent
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 31. Proof of Concept — Compressor Maintenance Agent
sections.content:
Create a synthetic Plant Ground-State with compressors, sensors and maintenance ownership.

Create a Jane intent for health monitoring and maintenance alerts.

Build the candidate Agent SPEC.

Resolve every compressor and sensor to Ground-State identifiers.

Bind a versioned ML Studio health model.

Bind the approved compressor SOP collection.

Bind a notification/maintenance-alert tool.

Explicitly deny PLC writes and setpoint changes.

Run schema and policy validation.

Replay normal telemetry.

Replay a high-risk vibration event.

Verify recommendation/alert behavior.

Replay the same event repeatedly and verify cooldown/idempotency.

Make telemetry stale and verify the SPEC blocks consequential action.

Make the model unavailable and verify declared fallback/escalation.

Attempt an unauthorized tool call and verify denial.

Hash/sign the SPEC.

Deploy the signed SPEC to a mock runtime.

Verify runtime refuses a modified SPEC.

100% asset references resolve.

0 unregistered tools.

0 unauthorized action permissions.

100% required schema checks pass.

All failure scenarios produce the declared behavior.

Stale data cannot silently produce a consequential action.

Unauthorized tool execution is rejected.

SPEC hash/signature verifies before runtime.

Modified SPEC is rejected.

Every deployment maps to exactly one immutable SPEC version.

All build, approval and runtime events are auditable.

This report is an engineering compliance/readiness assessment. It does not represent certification to ISO, NIST, IEC, regulatory or contractual requirements.

NIST AI RMF organizes risk management into Govern, Map, Measure and Manage and emphasizes continuous risk management throughout the AI lifecycle. The SPEC operationalizes these ideas as a concrete lifecycle artifact rather than treating governance as a separate document. citeturn0search10turn0search0

OWASP's current GenAI security project explicitly covers LLM and agentic AI systems and identifies risks such as prompt injection, insecure output handling, supply-chain vulnerabilities and excessive agency. citeturn0search2turn0search8

NIST AI RMF 1.0 provides a voluntary, risk-based framework for organizations designing, developing, deploying or using AI systems, with the goal of managing AI risks and supporting trustworthy AI. NIST also notes that the framework is being revised and that a Critical Infrastructure profile concept note was released in April 2026. citeturn0search4turn0search0

ISO 23247-2:2021 defines a manufacturing digital-twin reference architecture with domain/entity and functional views. AI-ConneX uses the same architectural principle of separating industrial entities/context from functions, with the Ground-State serving as the authoritative context reference for the Agent SPEC. citeturn0search1

OWASP's GenAI Security Project provides a practical security basis for the SPEC's separation of authority from model output, especially around prompt injection, insecure output handling, plugin/tool design and excessive agency. citeturn0search2turn0search3

Runtime MUST:1. Load only an approved SPEC.2. Verify signature/hash.3. Verify SPEC version.4. Resolve current policy.5. Verify Ground-State freshness.6. Enforce tool allow-list.7. Validate tool parameters.8. Enforce autonomy/action class.9. Request human approval where required.10. Enforce time/loop/rate limits.11. Audit every consequential operation.12. Stop if a mandatory precondition fails.

Runtime MUST NOT:

Invent permissions.

Expand asset scope.

Execute an unregistered tool.

Treat retrieved knowledge as authorization.

Silently replace a model version.

Bypass approval.

Ignore stale Ground-State conditions.

Continue after a fail-closed safety condition.

AGENT |RECOMMENDATION |CONSEQUENCE CLASSIFIER | +-- LOW --> AUTOMATED INFORM | +-- MEDIUM --> SUPERVISOR REVIEW | +-- HIGH --> EXPLICIT APPROVAL | +-- FORBIDDEN --> DENY

The SPEC makes the boundary explicit so the operator can understand whether the agent is informing, recommending, requesting authorization or executing.

The industrialist sees a clear contract instead of a hidden prompt.

Common agents can be deployed from templates.

Operational teams can review what the agent is allowed to do.

Safety teams can inspect action restrictions.

IT/security teams can inspect tools, identities and policies.

Data teams retain lineage through Data Studio references.

ML teams retain model ownership through ML Studio references.

Operations teams can see live execution against the same SPEC.

# schema validationpython -m agent_spec.validator validate schema/agent-spec.schema.json# validate examplepython -m agent_spec.validator validate examples/compressor.json# security checkspython -m agent_spec.security scan examples/compressor.json# scenario suitepython -m agent_spec.simulation run tests/scenarios/# compile signed artifactpython -m agent_spec.compiler compile examples/compressor.json   --output dist/agent-spec.jsonpython -m agent_spec.signer sign dist/agent-spec.json   --key-ref kms://agent-spec-signing# generate SBOMsyft dir:. -o cyclonedx-json > dist/sbom.json# verify artifactpython -m agent_spec.signer verify dist/agent-spec.json

Separate Builder and Runtime identities.

Separate development, staging and production SPEC registries.

Require two-person approval for high-consequence agents.

Use signed artifacts.

Store audit logs immutably.

Maintain SBOMs for the SPEC service and runtime.

Pin dependencies.

Run red-team tests for prompt injection and tool misuse.

Continuously test Ground-State freshness.

Monitor tool error rates and agent loop behavior.

Review SPECs after major model, tool or policy changes.

PROMPT = SUGGESTIONSPEC   = CONTRACTPOLICY = AUTHORITYRUNTIME = ENFORCEMENTTOOL GATEWAY = CONTROLLED SIDE EFFECTAUDIT = ACCOUNTABILITY

This separation is the central engineering decision. The Agent SPEC makes AI-ConneX's agent layer auditable and industrially governable without requiring the LLM itself to be trusted as the final authority.

USER | vJANE |  natural language intent vAGENT BUILDER |  compile vAGENT SPEC |  validate + sign vAPPROVAL / POLICY | vAGENT RUNTIME | | \__ MODEL | \__ KNOWLEDGE | \__ TELEMETRY | vTOOL GATEWAY | vINDUSTRIAL SYSTEM | vVISUALIZER | vINDUSTRIALISTData Studio -----------------> manifest/profile/DAG/feature refsML Studio -------------------> evaluated model refsVisualizer ------------------> Ground-State ref

NIST AI Risk Management Framework — official NIST resource. citeturn0search0turn0search4

ISO 23247-2:2021 — official ISO reference architecture page. citeturn0search1

OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications / GenAI Security Project. citeturn0search2turn0search3

NIST AI RMF Core — Govern, Map, Measure and Manage. citeturn0search10

Within AI-ConneX, the Agent SPEC should be treated as the constitutional document of an industrial agent. It freezes the intended purpose, context, capabilities, permissions, constraints, tests and provenance into a versioned artifact. This gives the Agent Runtime a precise contract and gives industrialists, operations, engineering, security and governance teams a common object to review.

The architecture therefore becomes: Jane defines intent → Agent Builder compiles it → Agent SPEC establishes the contract → Policy and approval establish authority → Runtime enforces the contract → Tool Gateway controls side effects → Visualizer exposes the operational result. Data Studio and ML Studio remain authoritative sources for data lineage and evaluated models respectively.

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > Chapter 19: Agentic Studio Agent Runtime Detailed Documentation
sections.content:
AI-ConneX

AGENTIC STUDIO — AGENT RUNTIME

Industrial Agent Execution PlaneR&D • Architecture • Failure Analysis • Implementation • POC • ComplianceReport #5 | Version 1.0 | 14 August 2026

The Agent Runtime is the controlled execution plane of AI-ConneX. It takes an approved, immutable Agent SPEC and turns it into observable runtime behavior: ingesting permitted observations, maintaining bounded state, invoking approved models and knowledge, planning within the SPEC, requesting approvals, calling only authorized tools, handling failures, escalating and recording an auditable execution trace.

The Runtime is deliberately NOT the Agent Builder and NOT the LLM. Builder creates the contract; the Runtime enforces it. The model may propose a next step, but the Runtime and Policy Engine decide whether that step is structurally permitted.

JANE  |  vAGENT BUILDER  |  vSIGNED AGENT SPEC  |  v+---------------------------+|       AGENT RUNTIME       ||                           || Trigger -> Observe ->     || Context -> Reason ->      || Validate -> Act -> Audit  |+-------------+-------------+              |       POLICY / APPROVAL              |        TOOL GATEWAY              |      INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS              |          VISUALIZER

sections.heading_text: 2. Why Runtime Is a Separate Stage
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 2. Why Runtime Is a Separate Stage
sections.content:
An LLM cannot safely be treated as an authorization layer.

Figure 19.1: Pipeline Connection — Agent Run-Time to RAG / Knowledge Base Engine

Industrial actions need deterministic enforcement.

Runtime state, retries, timeouts and concurrency need infrastructure controls.

Tools require credentials, network isolation and parameter validation.

Human approvals must pause and resume execution reliably.

Every consequential operation needs provenance and auditability.

Runtime must survive model/tool failures without inventing behavior.

This separation is directly aligned with the security concern of excessive agency: OWASP describes excessive functionality, permissions and autonomy as root causes and recommends constraining agent capabilities rather than relying on model behavior alone. citeturn0search1turn0search16

Research question: how can AI-ConneX execute an industrial agent continuously and reliably while keeping autonomy bounded by an explicit Agent SPEC, current industrial context, policy, model contracts and human approvals?

CHATBOT / JANE  intent_uid      |      vAGENT BUILDER  candidate -> validation -> signing      |      vAGENT SPEC  immutable contract      |      vAGENT RUNTIME  |   |   |   |   |  |   |   |   |   +-- Audit  |   |   |   +------ Approval  |   |   +---------- Tool Gateway  |   +-------------- Models / Knowledge  +------------------ Telemetry / Ground-State      |      vINDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS      |      vVISUALIZER / OPERATIONS

sections.heading_text: 5. What Runtime Receives from the Previous Stages
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 5. What Runtime Receives from the Previous Stages
sections.content: The Runtime should normally consume the signed Agent SPEC as its deployment contract. Upstream artifacts remain authoritative at their own layers and are referenced by immutable IDs rather than copied wholesale.

{  "spec_ref": "AGT-COMP-001:v1.0.0",  "spec_hash": "sha256:...",  "ground_state_ref": "GS-PLANT01:v18",  "model_refs": ["MODEL-COMP-HEALTH:v2.1.0"],  "manifest_uid": "MANIFEST-...",  "identity": {    "tenant_uid": "TENANT-01",    "principal": "operator/service"  },  "trigger": {    "type": "telemetry_event",    "event_uid": "EVT-..."  }}

EVENT / SCHEDULE      |      v1. AUTHENTICATE      |2. LOAD SPEC      |3. VERIFY SIGNATURE + HASH      |4. CHECK POLICY + SCOPE      |5. RESOLVE GROUND-STATE      |6. CHECK FRESHNESS      |7. BUILD CONTEXT      |8. INVOKE MODEL / RULES      |9. VALIDATE PROPOSED PLAN      |10. POLICY DECISION      |11. APPROVAL IF REQUIRED      |12. TOOL EXECUTION      |13. VERIFY RESULT      |14. UPDATE STATE      |15. AUDIT + TELEMETRY      |16. COMPLETE / RETRY / ESCALATE

CREATED  |VALIDATING  |READY  |RUNNING  |  | +--> WAITING_APPROVAL --> APPROVED --+  |                 |                    |  |                 +--> REJECTED -------+  |                                      |  +--> WAITING_DATA ---------------------+  |  +--> RETRYING  |  +--> ESCALATED  |  +--> FAILED  |  +--> COMPLETED  |  +--> TERMINATED

Only explicit state transitions are permitted. A state transition should carry an execution ID, SPEC version, reason and timestamp.

The LLM/model is a reasoning component, not the runtime authority. Its output must be converted into a typed internal representation before any tool call.

MODEL OUTPUT    |    vJSON / typed action plan    |    +--> schema validation    +--> scope validation    +--> policy validation    +--> parameter validation    +--> safety constraints    +--> approval check    |    vTOOL GATEWAY

All side-effecting operations should pass through a Tool Gateway. Credentials should remain outside prompts and outside the Agent SPEC wherever possible; the gateway maps a permitted capability to an appropriate service identity.

Agent Runtime     |     | typed ToolCall     vTool Gateway     |     +--> authenticate     +--> authorize     +--> validate schema     +--> validate asset scope     +--> idempotency     +--> rate limit     +--> execute     +--> capture result     |     vIndustrial API / Service

{  "tool_uid": "create_maintenance_alert",  "version": "1.3",  "capability": "inform",  "input_schema": "ALERT-V4",  "output_schema": "ALERT-RESULT-V2",  "side_effect": true,  "idempotency": "required",  "timeout_seconds": 20,  "allowed_autonomy": ["INFORM","RECOMMEND"]}

The Runtime needs an authoritative industrial context because an agent cannot safely reason about an asset from names alone. sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 37. Prompt Injection Defense at Runtime
sections.content:
Never concatenate retrieved instructions into an authorization context.

Keep system/SPEC/policy authority separate from untrusted content.

Treat model output as untrusted until validated.

Validate all tool arguments against typed schemas.

Apply policy after model planning and before side effects.

Limit tool capabilities to the SPEC.

Log injection detections and denied actions.

Use red-team regression scenarios.

sections.content:
Industrialists do not need to understand prompts or agent loops.

They see the asset, condition, evidence, recommendation, action and reason.

They can approve, reject, pause or escalate according to the SPEC.

Operations teams can inspect why an action was denied.

IT teams can inspect identity and audit trails.

Data teams can trace results back to Manifest/DAG/Family lineage.

ML teams can trace decisions to exact evaluated model versions.

The architectural boundary is deliberate: the Runtime is where the AI-ConneX agent becomes operational, but it never becomes unconstrained. The Agent SPEC defines the contract; policy and gateway enforce authority; the Runtime supplies durable execution, recovery and observability.

Agent Runtime is the execution heart of Agentic Studio. It converts the Agent SPEC from a static blueprint into a controlled, observable and recoverable industrial process. Its most important property is not autonomy; it is bounded autonomy.

For AI-ConneX, the complete chain is: Jane captures intent → Agent Builder compiles intent and industrial context → Agent SPEC defines the contract → Agent Runtime executes that contract → Policy/Approval controls authority → Tool Gateway controls side effects → Visualizer exposes the state → Audit preserves accountability.

That separation makes the architecture suitable for industrial environments where data quality, operational continuity, human accountability, security and traceability matter as much as model intelligence.

AI-ConneX

AGENTIC STUDIO — KNOWLEDGE & EXECUTION FOUNDATION

RAG • Knowledge Graph • Knowledge Base • Telemetry • Models • ToolsR&D • Failure Analysis • Architecture • POC • Compliance Report #5Version 1.0 | 14 August 2026

This stage is the information-and-capability foundation used by Agentic Studio. It does not simply give an LLM 'more data'. It creates six controlled planes: Knowledge Base for authoritative source material; RAG for semantic retrieval; Knowledge Graph for relationships and topology; Telemetry for time-sensitive operational state; Models for evaluated predictive/analytical capabilities; and Tools for bounded actions.

The design principle is: knowledge informs, telemetry contextualizes, models estimate, tools act, and the Agent SPEC + Policy decide what the Runtime is allowed to do.

AGENT SPEC                        |                        v                  AGENT RUNTIME                        |        +---------------+----------------+        |       CONTEXT ORCHESTRATOR     |        +---+---------+--------+---------+            |         |        |            RAG       KG    TELEMETRY            |         |        |           KB     topology   live state            |         |        |            +---------+--------+                      |                    MODELS                      |                 typed proposal                      |                    TOOLS                      |                Tool Gateway                      |                INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS

sections.heading_text: 2. Why Six Components Instead of One Vector Database
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 2. Why Six Components Instead of One Vector Database
sections.content:
A vector index alone cannot reliably represent current asset state, causal/structural relationships, authorization, or executable capabilities. AI-ConneX therefore treats retrieval, graph traversal, telemetry, inference and action as different contracts.

Figure 20.1: Pipeline Connection — RAG / KB Foundation to Agentic Tools

Industrial agents need answers that are simultaneously relevant, attributable, structurally correct, current, and actionable. Research therefore focuses on preventing five common substitutions: using similarity for truth, documents for live state, graph edges for causal certainty, model predictions for authorization, and tools as unrestricted functions.

Can retrieval be grounded to authoritative, versioned sources?

Can graph relationships complement semantic retrieval without becoming a hallucination amplifier?

Can live telemetry be freshness-aware and separated from static knowledge?

Can models be consumed through strict input/output contracts?

Can tools be capability-limited and policy-enforced?

Can all evidence and actions be traced to the exact agent execution?

Authority is explicit: source authority is metadata, not inferred from similarity.

Freshness is explicit: telemetry has timestamps, quality and maximum age.

Relationships are explicit: graph edges carry provenance and confidence.

Models are not authorities: predictions require model/version and context.

Tools are not knowledge: a tool is a capability with a schema and side-effect classification.

Untrusted retrieved text cannot change policy, permissions or SPEC.

Every result carries provenance sufficient for replay and audit.

Tenant/site/asset scope is applied before retrieval, graph traversal, inference or tool execution.

sections.heading_text: 5. Input From Previous Stage — Jane / Chatbot
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 5. Input From Previous Stage — Jane / Chatbot

sections.content: The signed SPEC is the contract. This stage cannot silently add a collection, model or tool.

The Knowledge Base is the authoritative source layer. It stores or references manuals, SOPs, maintenance records, engineering specifications, standards, incident reports, approved procedures and other governed material.

A KB record is not automatically trusted simply because it is indexed. Approval state, scope and provenance are evaluated before retrieval results become usable evidence.

SOURCE  -> connector  -> malware/file validation  -> parser/OCR  -> metadata extraction  -> classification  -> access-control tagging  -> chunking  -> embedding  -> lexical index  -> vector index  -> provenance registry  -> approval  -> published collection

Never overwrite a published document version; create a new immutable version.

Hash source content before processing.

Retain page/section/table identifiers where possible.

Mark obsolete documents as retired rather than deleting provenance.

Apply tenant and asset scope during ingestion, not only at query time.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is the evidence-retrieval mechanism. AI-ConneX uses hybrid retrieval rather than treating embeddings as the sole truth mechanism: lexical retrieval handles exact identifiers; vector retrieval handles semantic similarity; metadata filters enforce scope; reranking improves relevance; provenance determines whether content is eligible as evidence.

QUERY | +--> lexical search +--> vector search +--> metadata/security filter +--> optional KG expansion | +--> merge +--> rerank +--> freshness/authority check +--> evidence pack | vMODEL CONTEXT
OWASP's 2025 guidance explicitly treats Vector and Embedding Weaknesses as a security risk and separately warns that prompt injection is not eliminated by RAG. citeturn0search5turn0search6

The Knowledge Graph represents entities and relationships: plants, lines, machines, sensors, components, failure modes, maintenance procedures, models, datasets, alarms, work orders and dependencies. It answers structural questions that semantic search handles poorly.

Plant  -> contains -> Line  -> contains -> CompressorCompressor  -> hasSensor -> VibrationSensorCompressor  -> hasComponent -> BearingBearing  -> susceptibleTo -> FailureModeFailureMode  -> mitigatedBy -> ProcedureProcedure  -> documentedBy -> DocumentVersion

Graph relationships should carry provenance and, where appropriate, validity intervals. A graph edge is a represented relationship, not proof of causation.
Use stable UIDs and avoid natural-language names as primary identifiers.

User/Agent Intent      |      +--> KG: "What is connected to COMP-02?"      |       |      |       +--> sensor, component, procedure, model      |      +--> RAG: "What does the approved procedure say?"              |              +--> exact document sections                       |                       +--> combined evidence pack

The graph narrows the search space and supplies structural context; RAG supplies textual evidence. Neither is allowed to silently authorize actions.

Telemetry is fundamentally different from the KB: it describes changing state. AI-ConneX treats telemetry as time-series evidence with timestamp, source, quality, unit, sampling information and freshness.

A stale telemetry value must not be presented as current state. For consequential actions, freshness thresholds belong in the SPEC/policy.

PLC / SCADA / IoT Gateway        |     protocol adapter        |     message bus        | schema + unit validation        | quality / timestamp check        | time-series store        | feature/window service        | Ground-State / Agent Runtime

For manufacturing architectures, ISO 23247-2 defines a digital-twin reference architecture and ISO 23247-4 addresses information exchange between entities; these are useful standards anchors for separating observable manufacturing elements, digital-twin services and information exchange. citeturn0search1turn0search0

Models are controlled analytical capabilities. They may be predictive, classificatory, forecasting, anomaly-detection, physics-informed or multimodal. Runtime consumption is through a versioned model contract, not an informal prompt.

ML Studio supplies evaluated models and their lineage. The Knowledge layer stores references and documentation; the Runtime verifies the model contract before inference.

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 34. POC — Compressor Maintenance Knowledge Agent
sections.content:
Objective: answer and act on a compressor-maintenance request using all six planes while proving that the Runtime cannot exceed the Agent SPEC.

Load approved compressor manual v7 and maintenance SOP v4 into the KB.

Build graph entities for Plant-01, COMP-02, bearing, vibration sensor and approved procedures.

Stream vibration/temperature telemetry for COMP-02.

Register ML Studio's evaluated compressor-health model v2.1.0.

Register create_maintenance_alert v1.3 as an INFORM capability.

Create an Agent SPEC limiting evidence to Plant-01 and the compressor family.

Ask Jane: 'Watch COMP-02 and alert maintenance if bearing degradation is likely.'

Runtime resolves graph context and current telemetry.

RAG retrieves the approved bearing procedure.

Model produces a typed health estimate.

Runtime combines prediction + telemetry + graph + procedure evidence.

Tool Gateway creates an alert.

Replay the same event and verify no duplicate alert.

Insert a malicious instruction into a retrieved document and verify it cannot change tool permissions.

Make telemetry stale and verify the Runtime refuses the consequential action.

Attempt an unregistered work-order write tool and verify denial.

Inspect provenance and audit trace.

sections.heading_text: 38. What This Stage Does NOT Do
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 38. What This Stage Does NOT Do
sections.content:
It does not authorize industrial actions.

It does not override the Agent SPEC.

It does not treat retrieved text as instructions.

It does not turn telemetry into an action without Runtime/policy checks.

It does not deploy a model; ML Studio owns model training/evaluation.

It does not arbitrarily create tools.

It does not silently cross tenant/site/asset boundaries.

This makes an execution reproducible enough to answer: what did the agent know, what state did it observe, which model did it use, what capability did it invoke, and under which contract?
Targets are proposed starting points and should be calibrated against industrial workloads and network topology.

JANE  -> Intent UID  -> Agent Builder  -> Signed Agent SPEC  -> Agent Runtime       |       +--> Knowledge Base       |      -> authoritative documents       |       +--> RAG       |      -> relevant evidence       |       +--> Knowledge Graph       |      -> structural context       |       +--> Telemetry       |      -> current state       |       +--> Models       |      -> evaluated estimates       |       +--> Tools              -> bounded capabilities                    |                    v               Policy / Approval                    |                    v               Tool Gateway                    |                    v             Industrial Systems                    |             Audit + Visualizer

AI-ConneX should never ask a single component to be simultaneously a database, historian, ontology, predictor and actuator. The six-plane design makes each source good at its own job and forces the Agent Runtime to reconcile them under one explicit contract.

The resulting chain is: Jane expresses intent → Agent Builder formalizes it → Agent SPEC constrains it → Knowledge Foundation grounds it → Agent Runtime reasons and coordinates → Policy authorizes → Tools act → Telemetry observes the result → Audit closes the loop.

sections.heading_text: Chapter 21: Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > Chapter 21: Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture
sections.content:
AI-ConneX

DEPLOY & MONITOR PAGES

Unified Edge / Cloud Deployment, Serving, Observability & Industrial Runtime ArchitectureData Studio • ML Studio • Agentic StudioR&D → Failure Analysis → Architecture → POC → Compliance Report #5Version 1.0 | 14 August 2026

This document defines the AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages and the internal architecture that connects every approved artifact, model, recipe, manifest, agent, tool, telemetry stream and industrial endpoint into a deployable and observable runtime. The design supports edge, cloud and hybrid operation, with ONNX/ONNX Runtime for portable ML inference, MQTT for lightweight event/telemetry transport, REST APIs for synchronous application integration, and OPC UA where industrial equipment integration requires a standards-based industrial information model.

The central architectural principle is: BUILD ONCE → PACKAGE WITH IDENTITY → DEPLOY BY TARGET → VERIFY BEFORE SERVING → MONITOR CONTINUOUSLY → GOVERN CHANGES → ROLLBACK SAFELY.

ONNX Runtime is designed to run inference across cloud, edge and mobile environments and provides a common interface across multiple model frameworks and hardware accelerators. citeturn0search5turn0search9 MQTT 5.0 is a lightweight publish/subscribe protocol designed for constrained M2M/IoT environments. citeturn0search60 OPC UA provides industrial information models and communication mechanisms applicable to sensors, actuators, control systems, MES and ERP. citeturn0search6

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > 24. How the Architecture Overcomes Them
sections.content:
The architecture separates control plane from data plane. The control plane manages desired state, releases, policies and fleet identity. The data plane executes inference, agents and industrial connectivity locally or in the selected runtime. This allows edge operation without requiring continuous cloud connectivity.

Security follows zero-trust principles: no implicit trust based on network location; identity and authorization are evaluated for users, devices and services. NIST SP 800-207 explicitly recommends protecting resources rather than trusting network location, while SP 800-207A describes application/service identity, API gateways and service-identity mechanisms for cloud-native multi-cloud systems. citeturn0search0turn0search1

User / Device Identity        │   API Gateway / Edge Gateway        │ Authentication + Authorization        │ Service Identity / mTLS        │ Policy Enforcement Point        │ ┌──────▼──────────────────────────┐ │ Target Runtime                  │ │ Model • Agent • Tool • Data     │ └──────┬──────────────────────────┘        │ Continuous Telemetry + Audit        │ Policy / Detection / Response

mTLS between trusted runtime services.

Short-lived credentials where practical.

Tenant-scoped authorization.

Separate human identity from service identity.

Signed artifacts.

SBOM for deployable packages.

Secrets outside images.

Least-privilege tool access.

Network segmentation plus identity-based controls.

Audit all release and action decisions.
A tenant ID must never be accepted solely from a client-supplied body field. It should be derived from authenticated identity and server-side authorization context.

Pre-stage signed release bundles.

Cache model, feature recipe, agent package and required knowledge snapshot.

Continue local inference according to policy.

Buffer telemetry locally with bounded retention.

Queue non-critical cloud actions.

Block actions that explicitly require central approval.

On reconnection, reconcile telemetry and deployment state.

Detect conflicting desired state before applying updates.

Deployment produces a live Release/Runtime State that becomes the input to continuous monitoring. Monitor then feeds telemetry, incidents and evidence back into Jane and, where policy allows, into controlled retraining/redeployment workflows.

This is a design-stage compliance report, not a certification. Production compliance requires implementation evidence, penetration/security testing, operational validation, applicable industrial standards review and organization-specific regulatory/legal review.

sections.heading_text: Chapter 22: Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-022 > Chapter 22: Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan
sections.content:
AI-ConneX

MULTI-TENANCY IMPLEMENTATION & STUDIO DEPLOYMENT PLAN

R&D → Architecture → Isolation → Deployment → POC → Compliance Report #5Version 1.0 | 14 August 2026

AI-ConneX is designed as an industrial multi-studio platform. Multi-tenancy must therefore be implemented as a platform-wide security and data-governance property, not as a UI feature added to individual Studios. Every request, dataset, manifest, DAG, recipe, model, agent, telemetry stream, visualization, tool call, audit event and deployment must carry an authenticated tenant context and must be authorized against it.

The recommended baseline is a hybrid isolation model: shared application services with strict tenant-scoped authorization and database Row-Level Security for standard tenants; dedicated databases/namespaces/storage/keys for regulated or high-isolation tenants. This follows the principle that tenant context must be derived from verified identity, not trusted from a client-supplied header, and that isolation should exist at multiple layers. OWASP's current multi-tenant guidance explicitly calls out cross-tenant leakage, IDOR, cache/session isolation, noisy neighbors, onboarding/offboarding and audit gaps as core risks. citeturn0search1

The deployment plan uses zero-trust principles: network location is not the authorization boundary; authenticated user/service identity and resource attributes are. NIST SP 800-207 and SP 800-207A provide the architectural basis for identity-centric authorization in distributed/cloud-native systems. citeturn0search4turn0search2

A tenant is an independently governed industrial organization or organizational boundary whose users, data, assets, models, agents, policies and audit records must be isolated from other tenants. A tenant may contain multiple sites, plants, business units, environments and asset families.

Tenant├── Users / Groups / Service Identities├── Sites│   ├── Plants│   └── Asset Families├── Data Assets├── Manifests / DAGs / Recipes├── Features / Models├── Agents / Agent SPECs├── Knowledge Base / RAG / Graph├── Telemetry├── Tool permissions├── Deployments├── Policies├── Audit / Billing / Quotas└── Retention / Compliance settings

Confidentiality: Tenant A cannot read Tenant B resources.

Integrity: Tenant A cannot modify Tenant B resources.

Execution isolation: tenant-scoped jobs cannot execute against another tenant.

Knowledge isolation: RAG, graph and retrieval cannot cross tenant boundaries unless explicitly configured for shared public knowledge.

Agent isolation: Main Agents and Toolkit calls inherit tenant scope.

Telemetry isolation: live and historical industrial data remains tenant-scoped.

Cache isolation: keys always include tenant and resource scope.

Storage isolation: object paths/buckets are tenant-scoped.

Observability isolation: operators see only permitted tenant traces/logs.

Administrative isolation: platform administrators require explicit break-glass procedures for cross-tenant operations.

Offboarding: tenant data can be retained, exported and deleted according to policy.

PostgreSQL RLS should be treated as defense in depth rather than the only control. OWASP recommends database-level isolation plus application/data-access authorization, tenant-scoped composite lookups, cache/storage isolation and per-tenant quotas. citeturn0search1
The tier is a deployment policy. It should not change the application authorization contract: every service still receives and validates tenant context.

{  "tenant_uid": "TEN-7f8...",  "org_uid": "ORG-...",  "user_uid": "USR-...",  "roles": ["TENANT_ADMIN"],  "site_scope": ["SITE-01"],  "asset_scope": ["COMP-*"],  "environment": "prod",  "policy_version": "POL-12"}

Tenant context is generated from a verified identity/token and server-side membership lookup. A client may request a site or tenant, but the server determines whether the authenticated principal has that scope. OWASP specifically recommends deriving tenant context from authenticated sessions and not trusting client-supplied tenant IDs. citeturn0search1

AI-ConneX should combine RBAC with ABAC/ReBAC-style attributes. Role answers 'what class of operation?', while attributes answer 'on which tenant/site/asset/environment?'. OWASP notes that ABAC can better represent multi-organizational access patterns than role-only designs. citeturn0search0

ALLOW if:identity.validAND identity.activeAND tenant_membership(identity, tenant)AND resource.tenant_uid == tenant.uidAND site in identity.site_scopeAND asset in identity.asset_scopeAND action in role.permissionsAND policy.allows(action, resource, context)

CLIENT  |API Gateway / WAF  |  authenticate  vTenant Context Middleware  |Authorization / Policy  |Service-to-Service Identity  |Repository / Query Scope  |Database RLS  |Storage / Cache / Queue Scope  |Audit + Monitoring

The decisive authorization check is server-side. UI filtering is only a usability feature. OWASP's authorization guidance explicitly recommends server-side enforcement, deny-by-default and authorization tests. citeturn0search0

The implementation should make this rule structural rather than procedural: developers should have to consciously create an exception rather than remember to add a tenant filter.

Multi-tenancy is the platform foundation that makes AI-ConneX suitable for multiple industrial organizations. The key architectural decision is not merely 'add tenant_id'; it is to propagate authenticated tenant context through the entire lifecycle—from Jane's intent, through Data Studio's artifacts and ML Studio's models, into Agentic Studio's SPEC/runtime/knowledge/toolkit, and finally into every operational action and audit record.

The recommended implementation combines application authorization, database isolation, storage/cache/vector/graph/telemetry scoping, service identity, network controls, quotas, auditability and continuous cross-tenant testing. This defense-in-depth model aligns with current OWASP multi-tenant guidance and NIST zero-trust principles. citeturn0search1turn0search2

TAS | AI-ConneX — Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan End-of-Stage Verification

The AI-ConneX platform provides a complete, production-ready, and data-centric solution for industrial artificial intelligence. By establishing three independent, contract-bound studios—Data Studio, ML Studio, and Agentic Studio—the platform overcomes the primary failure modes of traditional AI systems: silent data corruption, unvalidated feature leakage, non-deterministic execution, and unsafe LLM tool usage. Through the implementation of the Brain cognitive layers, the S.T.E.M. model execution spine, immutable Agent SPEC blueprints, quarantined PREPARE pipelines, and multi-tenant Kubernetes isolation, AI-ConneX delivers an end-to-end architecture that guarantees physical safety, operational resilience, and enterprise compliance.
